claims.claim: The roadmap records a standing scope commitment that ordered or automated deletion of ApplicationSet children "will not be implemented" and that teardown "remains a manual operator action, performed one Application at a time", while the PRD proposes exactly that capability as a new spec.strategy.deletionOrder field with a Reverse value that deletes in the reverse of the rollingSync step order and waits for each Application to be fully deleted before the next. Shipping the PRD reverses a recorded roadmap exclusion; nothing in either document acknowledges the other, so the reversal would land without ever being argued.

The PRD's deletionOrder work has no named decider: its sponsors, reviewers and approvers are all TBD, yet it overturns the roadmap's explicit out-of-scope line on ApplicationSet child deletion. The only place the contradiction is even raised is a raw incident-review note that says the question "needs an owner. not deciding here." On current record the roadmap commitment is being informed of the change after the fact rather than anyone with authority deciding to drop it.

Displaced work, named: the roadmap states application controller capacity this quarter is committed to the Progressive Sync Stable-promotion punch list and that the pair who owns "Sharding application controller" is the same pair working that list, so sharding does not start until Stable promotion closes. The Stable-promotion ticket defines its remaining scope only as open backlog queries for progressive-sync bugs and enhancements, with no enumerated exit list, so the date sharding unblocks is set by an unbounded queue. Automatic controller scaling for high availability is the specific work that slips, and it slips for as long as that queue stays open.

Displaced work, named: the platform sync call deprioritized the hydrator History & Rollback ticket to next quarter and moved the dev pair onto the progressive sync deletion loop. The capability being given up is precisely the one the new work creates demand for. The rollback ticket is the only proposed mechanism for reverting a hydrated sync branch, and the Reverse deletion strategy deletes Applications one at a time waiting on each, so a teardown that stalls partway leaves the hydrated branch with no automated way back.

The platform sync call recorded as "a real decision, not a maybe" that impersonation rollout goes behind a per-project flag rather than fleet-wide, but the impersonation RFC's goals state the feature "can be enabled/disabled only at the system level" and that once enabled it applies to all Argo CD Applications, with the control surfaces being the argocd-cm key, the ARGOCD_APPLICATION_CONTROLLER_ENABLE_IMPERSONATION environment variable and the --enable-impersonation flag. The gating mechanism the decision depends on does not exist in the design it is meant to govern, so the decision as recorded cannot be enforced.

The rollout precondition "nobody flips it on a project until the diff story is fixed" is already broken in the field: the CI diff bug reports failures in "projects where we recently enabled the sync impersonation flag", and the diff story it was conditioned on is still open, with Server-Side Diff on external clusters running as the cluster Secret credential instead of the AppProject destinationServiceAccounts identity. The bet was priced on a hold that is not being observed, so the exposure the hold was meant to defer is being taken now.

The evidence that would show the Stable-promotion bet is wrong is not observable before it is paid for. The progressive sync bug report states plainly that there is no counter incrementing when specChanged fires without a resulting sync operation, so the pilot fleet's silent-rollout-failure rate is a count of support pings rather than a measured rate. The ticket proposing exactly the missing instrumentation (time to trigger, time per step, refreshes caused, what a stalled sync is waiting on) sits in the enhancement backlog and is not named in the Stable promotion scope, so promotion can be declared on an unmeasured failure mode.

Succeeding at Reverse deletion forecloses the parallel-steps direction. The PRD states Reverse assumes rollingSync.steps stays a strictly sequential list of match groups, one deployed and deleted at a time, for as long as the feature exists, and that any change letting a step contain more than one match group evaluated concurrently removes the single ordering Reverse depends on. The parallel progressive sync steps ticket proposes precisely that, a parallel list of matchExpressions per step so independent cluster groups stop blocking each other. The Stable promotion scope call freezes the steps shape as the v1 backward-compatibility bar and requires any change to how a step is expressed to land as a new field before that point, so shipping Reverse and then promoting to Stable closes the window on the parallelism request without either document citing the other.

The roadmap direction that ApplicationSet destroy ordering unlocks is the same combination currently interdicted operationally. The Source Hydrator for ApplicationSets request wants hydrated Applications so sync waves can control destroy order across multiple ApplicationSets, but the incident review's standing interim rule is that hydrator pilot repos must not use progressive sync until there is a debounce, because each hydrator push restarts the rolling sync wave. Building ordered teardown on top of the hydrator therefore has a prerequisite nobody has scheduled: the debounce. Without it, the success case is a configuration operators are currently told not to run.
